# Flutter Mobile Application Security (MOB)

The device and the app package must be treated as hostile: a rooted phone can read the app's files, hook its code and change its logic. Every security decision made in the app needs a server-side check. Controls in this domain reduce risk on the device; they never replace server controls.

## SCS-MOB-01 Store tokens and credentials only in platform secure storage

Level: MUST

Applies to: Flutter mobile

Policy: Authentication tokens, credentials and keys MUST be stored only in flutter_secure_storage (Android Keystore / iOS Keychain). SharedPreferences, plain files, unencrypted databases and logs MUST NEVER be used for them. Passwords MUST NOT be stored on the device at all.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Use flutter_secure_storage (current major version). On iOS use KeychainAccessibility.first_unlock_this_device (or unlocked_this_device) with synchronizable: false.
- Keep the access token in memory; store only the refresh token.
- Plan for loss: secure storage can be reset (resetOnError, backup restores); the app must always allow a fresh sign-in.
- iOS Keychain items survive uninstall: on first launch after install, clear old items using a flag in normal preferences.
- Upgrading flutter_secure_storage from 9.x: ship a 10.x build first so stored data migrates, then 11.x.

Verification: Grep for SharedPreferences used with token, jwt, refresh or password. MASTG storage test on a rooted test device: no tokens in shared_prefs, databases or files.

## SCS-MOB-02 Minimize and encrypt sensitive data on the device, and wipe it on logout

Level: MUST

Applies to: Flutter mobile

Policy: Sensitive business or personal data MUST NOT be stored in plain text on the device. Keep as little as possible; data that must be cached MUST be encrypted with a key held in secure storage, kept in app-private storage, and wiped on logout. Temporary files and caches holding sensitive data MUST be deleted as soon as they are no longer needed.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Local databases with sensitive data: SQLCipher through package:sqlite3 (build hook source: sqlcipher) with drift, or Hive with encryptionCipher. The key comes from Random.secure() and is stored in flutter_secure_storage. sqflite, Hive (unencrypted) and files are plain text by default.
- Use getApplicationSupportDirectory / getTemporaryDirectory (app-private). Never external storage for sensitive data.
- Delete camera/picker temporary files and downloaded documents in a finally block after use.
- Android: android:allowBackup="false", plus dataExtractionRules (API 31+) that exclude cloud backup and device-transfer, and fullBackupContent for API 30 and below.
- On logout and on account switch: delete the database, caches, temporary files and secure storage entries.

Verification: MASTG storage tests: inspect the app sandbox on a test device after use and after logout; confirm adb backup returns no app data.

## SCS-MOB-03 Prevent leakage through the screen, clipboard and keyboard

Level: MUST

Applies to: Flutter mobile

Policy: Screens that show sensitive data MUST block screenshots and screen recording and hide their content in the app switcher. Sensitive input fields MUST disable suggestions, autocorrect and keyboard learning. The app MUST NOT copy secrets to the clipboard.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Android: set FLAG_SECURE on sensitive screens (early in onCreate, or per route with a package such as screen_protector) and set filterTouchesWhenObscured for tapjacking protection.
- iOS: blur or cover the screen when the app becomes inactive (for example screen_protector.protectDataLeakageWithBlur()).
- TextField(obscureText: true, enableSuggestions: false, autocorrect: false, enableIMEPersonalizedLearning: false) for passwords, PINs and OTPs.
- Do not call Clipboard.setData with secrets; Android 13+ shows a preview of copied text.

Verification: Manual test on Android and iOS: screenshots blocked, app-switcher preview hidden, no keyboard suggestions on sensitive fields.

## SCS-MOB-04 Pin backend certificates safely

Level: MUST

Applies to: Flutter mobile

Policy: Mobile apps MUST pin the backend APIs we control to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks. Pins MUST target the issuing CA (or intermediate) public key, not the leaf certificate, and MUST include at least one backup pin. The app MUST have a forced-update path for when pins change.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Use SecurityContext(withTrustedRoots: false) with setTrustedCertificatesBytes() loaded with our issuing CA and a backup CA, applied to the HttpClient used by package:http (IOClient) or dio.
- Public TLS certificates now last at most 200 days (falling to 47 days by 2029), so leaf pins break often; never pin the leaf.
- Coordinate certificate and CA changes with Infrastructure, and release the app with the new pin before the server certificate changes.
- Test pinning on iOS as well as Android; some SecurityContext behavior differs on iOS.
- Pinning does not replace normal certificate validation (SCS-CRY-01).

Verification: MASTG network test: intercept with a proxy using a user-installed CA and confirm the app refuses to connect.

## SCS-MOB-05 Bind biometric and local authentication to a cryptographic key

Level: MUST

Applies to: Flutter mobile

Policy: Biometric or device-PIN checks that unlock sensitive features MUST be bound to a key in the Android Keystore / iOS Keychain that requires user authentication. A plain true/false result from a biometric prompt MUST NOT be the only gate, as it can be bypassed on a rooted device. The server still validates whatever token or signature is released.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Use flutter_secure_storage biometric options (AndroidOptions with enforceBiometrics and strong biometrics only) or a BiometricPrompt + CryptoObject plugin; on iOS a Keychain item with SecAccessControl .biometryCurrentSet.
- Add NSFaceIDUsageDescription to Info.plist and use FlutterFragmentActivity on Android.
- Do not use local_auth.authenticate() alone to release secrets or approve transactions.

Verification: Code review confirms the secret is released only by the OS after biometric authentication.

## SCS-MOB-06 Lock down deep links, WebViews and platform channels

Level: MUST

Applies to: Flutter mobile

Policy: Deep links MUST use verified Android App Links / iOS Universal Links, and every parameter MUST be validated. A deep link MUST NOT perform a state-changing action without user confirmation. WebViews MUST have JavaScript disabled unless the content is trusted, MUST allow-list navigation, and MUST NOT load untrusted HTML. Platform channel and native plugin code MUST validate all input. Android components MUST be exported only when needed.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Android: <intent-filter android:autoVerify="true"> with https, and /.well-known/assetlinks.json listing the signing SHA-256 (Play App Signing key). iOS: applinks: entitlements, not CFBundleURLSchemes. Flutter deep linking is on by default; turn it off (flutter_deeplinking_enabled) if not used.
- Validate deep-link parameters (int.tryParse, allow-lists) and route to a confirmation screen for any action.
- webview_flutter: setJavaScriptMode(JavaScriptMode.disabled) by default; a NavigationDelegate that allows only https and approved hosts; on Android setAllowFileAccess(false) and setAllowContentAccess(false); enableDebugging only in debug builds. A JavaScriptChannel receives no origin, so any page loaded can call it.
- Platform channels: validate type, range and length on the native side; never expose generic exec, readFile(path) or rawQuery(sql) methods; prefer Pigeon for typed channels.
- Set android:exported explicitly on every component; review the merged AndroidManifest (plugins add components and permissions).

Verification: adb shell pm get-app-links <package> shows verified links. Review of the merged manifest and WebView settings. Test malformed deep links.

## SCS-MOB-07 Harden release builds

Level: MUST

Applies to: Flutter mobile

Policy: Release builds MUST be built in release mode with obfuscation, signed with the production key (never the debug key), contain no debug features, test endpoints or debug logging, request only the permissions they need, and target current platform versions. Build-time debug relaxations MUST be behind compile-time flags that are never set for production.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Build with flutter build appbundle / ipa --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=<folder outside the repo>; keep symbol files private for crash symbolization.
- Android release signingConfig uses the upload key from CI secrets, never signingConfigs.debug (the Flutter template default).
- No android:debuggable, no usesCleartextTraffic="true", no user-installed CAs outside debug-overrides in network_security_config.
- Keep permissions minimal; avoid MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, READ/WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES and SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW unless approved.
- Target the current Google Play target API level and a supported minimum OS version; enforce a minimum app version from the server (forced update) for security fixes.
- Use --dart-define compile-time flags (not kDebugMode) for any staging-only behavior, because QA builds are usually release builds.

Verification: Release checklist: check the signing certificate (apksigner verify --print-certs), the merged manifest, permissions and the obfuscation flags in the pipeline.

## SCS-MOB-08 Add runtime protection for high-risk apps

Level: SHOULD

Applies to: Flutter mobile

Policy: Apps classified as High risk SHOULD detect rooted or jailbroken devices, debuggers, hooking frameworks and tampering, and SHOULD use platform attestation (Play Integrity / App Attest) verified on the server. These are defense-in-depth measures only and MUST NOT replace server-side controls.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Consider freeRASP or a similar RASP SDK; get a privacy review first, as such SDKs may send device data to their vendor.
- Verify Play Integrity / Firebase App Check tokens on the server (nonce, requestHash, app and device integrity verdicts). Never ship debug attestation providers.
- Decide the response (warn, limit features, block) per app in the threat model.

Verification: Test on a rooted/jailbroken device and with Frida attached; confirm the planned response occurs.
